newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australians drinking less beer, more soft drinks, milk.
newsitem.headline: Australians drinking less beer, more soft drinks, milk.

text.p: Official figures released on Friday dealt another blow to the image of Australians as devout beer drinkers.
Australians on average actually consume more soft drinks and milk than beer, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said.

Total beer consumption declined for the seventh successive year with a fall of 1.6 percent to 95.4 litres (21 gallons) a person in the year ended June 30, 1996, it said. Consumption of low alcohol beer rose 4.7 percent to 22.4 litres (4.9 gallons) a head in 1995/96 but that of other beer fell 3.4 percent to 73.0 litres (16 gallons), the bureau said.
Australians drank 114.3 litres (25 gallons) each of soft drinks in 1995/96, up 3.3 percent on the previous year, in the fourth consecutive annual increase.
Milk consumption rose for the third successive year to 104.3 litres (23 gallons) per person.
However, the consumption of tea and coffee remained steady at 0.9 kg (two pounds) of tea and 2.2 kg (4.8 pounds) of coffee per head, the bureau said.
